title: The factor of $250$: why color superconductivity is inaccessible at nuclear densities
html: Factor of 250. The ratio 746.4 / 3.016 \approx 247 between Borromean and Hopf binding at q = q_0 (energy crossover) shows why color superconductivity remains inaccessible at nuclear densities. The compression energy must supply roughly 750 Skein units per baryon to close the gap. This demands densities many times \rho_0. This conclusion matches QCD estimates, which place the CFL onset at \rho \gtrsim 5\text{--}10\rho_0, deep inside neutron star cores.
